summary: Frontend-only UI testing of media (image/video/document) uploads after Emergent Object Storage migration, on both /send (SendMessagesSimple) and /my-templates (MyTemplates), plus oversize/wrong-type validation and campaign-creation regression. Logged in as qatest@example.com. RESULT: /send flows fully pass (all 3 types upload, URL populated, public URL returns 200 with correct content-type: image/jpeg, video/mp4, application/pdf). /my-templates image+video pass and persist, but DOCUMENT upload does NOT populate the document URL field (confirmed reproducible in isolation) - React stale-state bug in MyTemplates.js. Campaign regression with uploaded image header passes (campaign created, visible in Campaign History at /campaigns).

ui_bugs.issue: After uploading a PDF in the template dialog with Media Type = Document, the 'Or paste document URL' field stays EMPTY while the filename field is filled with 'test_doc.pdf'. Saving therefore persists header_document = '' (document lost). Root cause: MediaUploader calls onHeaderDocumentChange(url) and onHeaderDocumentNameChange(fileName) back-to-back in the same tick, and MyTemplates passes non-functional object-spread setters ({...formData, header_document: v} then {...formData, header_document_name: v}) - the second call uses stale formData and wipes the just-set URL. Fix: use functional updates, e.g. setFormData(f => ({...f, header_document: v})) for ALL MediaUploader setters in MyTemplates.js (lines ~294-308). /send is unaffected because it uses individual useState setters.

issues: The 'Document filename' input has no visible Label (only a placeholder), so once filled with e.g. 'test_doc.pdf' it looks like a stray unlabeled field below the URL input. Add a Label for clarity.

action_items: MyTemplates.js: convert all MediaUploader onChange handlers to functional setFormData updates so the document URL is not overwritten by the subsequent filename update (HIGH - document media is silently dropped when saving a template).
Optional: add a Label to the document filename input in MediaUploader.jsx.
critical_code_review_comments: MyTemplates.js: handleFileUpload (lines 147-154) is dead code - MediaUploader performs the upload itself via useMediaUpload; the page-level uploadFile/uploading hook is only used for the submit button disabled state. Remove or consolidate to avoid two upload paths.

MyTemplates.js uses stale-closure object-spread setState for every MediaUploader callback; any pair of setters fired in the same tick will lose data (document URL case proven). Prefer functional updates everywhere.

MediaUploader: no client-side MIME/extension pre-check - a .txt selected under 'Image' is only rejected by the backend (400). Error toast is clear ('Invalid file type. Allowed: .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif, .webp') and no URL is set, so behaviour is acceptable but a client-side check would save a round trip.

rca_of_the_issue: Document URL lost in /my-templates: MediaUploader.handleFileChange calls onHeaderDocumentChange(result.url) immediately followed by onHeaderDocumentNameChange(result.fileName). In MyTemplates.js both props are inline closures over the current `formData` object ({...formData, header_document: v}). React batches both setState calls, so the second one starts from the pre-upload `formData` snapshot (header_document = '') and overwrites the URL set by the first. Reproduction: /my-templates -> New Template -> Media Type 'Document' -> upload any PDF -> URL field empty, filename field populated. Mitigation: functional setState updates in MyTemplates.js.
